title: Committee of Supply – Head X (Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head X (Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth)

sections.label: MCCY COS debate motion
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce Head X of the Estimates by $100, opening the MCCY Committee of Supply debate, referencing Singapore's 60th year of nation-building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head X of the Estimates be reduced by $100." To kick off the Committee of Supply (COS) debate for the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) this year, I want to take reference from the fact that 2025 marks the 60th year of Singapore's nation-building.

sections.label: Aid for Gaza fundraising
sections.summary: The M3 fundraising effort Aid for Gaza collected over $166,000 in one week, uniting residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The M3 fundraising effort for Gaza, Aid for Gaza, successfully united residents, collecting over $166,000 in just one week.

sections.label: M3 community health focus
sections.summary: M3 Community Health Focus was introduced in 2023 to encourage the Malay/Muslim community to own their health, and M3 marked its fifth anniversary last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To what extent is the Government working with M3@Towns to optimise community assets, workforce and volunteers to maximise the impact of M3 programmes across various areas? :   The M3 Community Health Focus was introduced in 2023 to encourage the Malay/Muslim community to take ownership of their health and adopt healthy lifestyles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on the health outcomes of the Malay/Muslim community and how Focus Area 3, in promoting community health, has contributed to this improvement?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in Malay, please. :   M3 celebrated its fifth anniversary last year.

sections.label: Woodlands Health Club exercise groups
sections.summary: M3 established the Woodlands Health Club, a programme for exercise interest groups including Jalan Kakis, Trekking, Zumba A Go Go, Piloxing, Kampung Cycle and Football, with Yoga and Gym Buddies soon.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At M3, we have established the Woodlands Health Club, a programme for various exercise interest groups, including Jalan Kakis, Trekking, Zumba A Go Go, Piloxing, Kampung Cycle, Football, and soon, we will be starting Yoga and Gym Buddies.

sections.label: Project Dian rental flat support
sections.summary: Project Dian, introduced in 2021, supports low-income Malay/Muslim families in rental flats through targeted assistance and community guidance, and expanded to more M3@Towns in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Project Dian, which was first introduced in 2021, plays an important role in supporting low-income Malay/Muslim families living in rental flats through targeted assistance and community guidance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With its expansion to more M3@Towns in 2023, it is timely to assess its impact and future direction.

sections.label: Project Dian expansion and asatizah roles
sections.summary: A question asks whether Project Dian will expand to all M3@Towns or have assistance enhanced, and notes asatizah also guide social and community matters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Furthermore, with the rising costs of living, are there plans to further expand Project Dian to all other M3@Towns or to enhance the types of assistance provided? :   Sir, asatizah not only play a role as religious educators but also provide guidance on social and community matters.

sections.label: Mosque Executive Chairman management
sections.summary: Asks how many mosques are managed by Executive Chairmen versus non-Executive Chairmen, noting MUIS pays 20% of the Executive Chairman's salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My first question: how many mosques are currently under the management of Executive Chairmen (MEC) and how many are under the management of non-Executive Chairmen?

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: During the 2012 Committee of Supply debates, in replying to my query, the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs at that time said that MUIS bears or pays 20% of the Executive Chairman's monthly salary and the remainder is paid by the mosque.

sections.label: Warees Halal revenue and plans
sections.summary: Asks for Warees Halal's annual revenue, expenses and net income from 2020 to 2024 and its medium-term plans for halal services demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My questions are as follows: (i) what are the annual revenue, expenses and net income of Warees Halal between 2020 to 2024; and (ii) what are Warees Halal’s plans to meet the increasing demand for halal services in the medium term?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: In Malay, please, :   Mr Chairman, in response to a Parliamentary Question in 2023 regarding plans to build new mosques following cost increases due to COVID-19, it was stated that these plans needed to be reassessed due to the pandemic's impact on construction costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Now, with construction costs stabilising and a growing population in Tampines and Pasir Ris due to new BTO developments, I am pleased to hear that the construction of the mosque in Tampines North will proceed.

sections.label: HashTech and Professional Networks
sections.summary: States that HashTech volunteers mentor youths in dashboarding, data analytics and generative AI, and that 13 Professional Networks were established.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: In our annual HashTech programme, volunteers from the technology industry mentor youths in dashboarding, data analytics and generative AI, helping them build skills and develop skills portfolios through hackathons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: We have established 13 Professional Networks, including engineering, technology, law and healthcare.

sections.label: Mentoring programme effectiveness tracking
sections.summary: Asks about success and participation rates of mentoring programmes, how they help youths explore industries, and whether effectiveness is tracked.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Given the many mentoring programmes that help Malay/Muslim youths build professional networks and explore new industries, I would like to ask, firstly, what are the success and participation rates for these programmes; how have these mentoring programmes helped our youths explore new industries and employment opportunities; and is the programmes’ effectiveness being tracked?

sections.label: Tunas initiative inclusivity
sections.summary: Asks how inclusive the Tunas initiative is in reaching Malay/Muslim youths by gender, age and educational background.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share how inclusive the Tunas initiative is in reaching out to various groups of our Malay/Muslim youths in terms of gender, age, and educational background? :   We must continue our efforts to support and strengthen our young Malay/Muslim couples and families.

sections.label: KMM parents and children
sections.summary: States more than 10,000 parents and children benefited from KMM, and in 2023 about 450 KMM completers celebrated two decades with Mendaki.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: More than 10,000 parents and children have benefited from KMM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In 2023, I celebrated the success and achievements of this programme's two decades together with Mendaki at Temasek Polytechnic, with around 450 parents and children who had completed the KMM programme.

sections.label: Madrasah Aljunied IB diploma report
sections.summary: It was reported that Madrasah Aljunied Al-Islamiah was the only madrasah offering the International Baccalaureate diploma in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, it was reported that Madrasah Aljunied Al-Islamiah was the only madrasah to offer the International Baccalaureate (IB) diploma in Singapore. : Mr Chairman, please allow me to continue in English.

sections.label: Worker initiatives and Singapore Islamic College
sections.summary: The Government introduced SkillsFuture, Career Conversion Programmes and upskilling schemes, and the Prime Minister announced the Singapore Islamic College.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The Government has introduced various initiatives, such as SkillsFuture, Career Conversion Programmes and sector-specific upskilling schemes, to help workers transition into higher-value industries and digital-driven roles.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Additionally, how can we further strengthen community partnerships, mentorship networks and career guidance programmes to help workers navigate industry changes and seize new economic opportunities? :   Last year, the Prime Minister announced the establishment of the Singapore Islamic College (SCIS), marking a significant milestone in our efforts to develop a future-ready pipeline of asatizah.

sections.label: Outreach to Muslims in Singapore
sections.summary: In five months, over 2,000 participants were reached at physical events and nearly 340,000 online impressions, about 50% of Muslims in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In just five months, we reached out to over 2,000 participants in physical events and nearly 340,000 online impressions, approximately 50% of all Muslims in Singapore.

sections.label: Legacy planning and WMS fundraising
sections.summary: It asks about plans to equip the community for legacy planning and WMS contributions, and for an update on WMS fundraising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: What are the plans to equip the community with the knowledge and skills to do legacy planning and contribute to WMS?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Can the Minister also provide an update on the fundraising efforts and funds raised through WMS thus far?

sections.label: Malay/Muslim community SG60 contributions
sections.summary: It asks about Malay/Muslim contributions to SG60, citing tudung handling, mosque closures and MUIS, and proposing leadership in growth areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Can the Minister share more about the Malay/Muslim community's contributions to the SG60 celebrations this year?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: First, we can be the shining example of how the Malay/Muslim community can progress in harmony with other groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The calibrated manner in which we handled the tudung issue over the years, the mature way in which we accepted the closure of mosques during the COVID-19 pandemic and how MUIS addressed various issues – all these are not as easily achieved in many other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Second, we should take the lead in developing global thought leadership in growth areas, such as Islamic finance, Shariah-compliant medical treatments and bio-medicine, sustainable finance, as well as climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: How can our community contribute to building a shared Singapore future together in a sustained way?

sections.label: FA5 health initiatives with M3
sections.summary: Since FA5 began, M3 worked with HPB and partners on health initiatives, expanding Saham Kesihatan to 11 M3@Towns and growing JKJU participation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Since we started FA5 two years ago, M3 have collaborated with the Health Promotion Board (HPB) and our community partners on many initiatives to improve the health of Malay/Muslims, including in the areas of active ageing and mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We expanded the Saham Kesihatan initiative to all 11 M3@Towns, and more than 800 individuals joined in 2024, up from over 500 individuals in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: JKJU participants increased from over 4,000 participants in 2023 to nearly 70,000 participants last year.

sections.label: Malay enrolment increase
sections.summary: Enrolment among Malays rose from 30% in May 2024 to 45% in February 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Enrolment among Malays increased from 30% in May 2024 to 45% in February 2025.

sections.label: Malay chronic disease screening rate
sections.summary: Only 53% of Malays aged 40 to 74 attended chronic disease screening in 2023, leaving room for improvement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The participation rate of Malay/Muslims in chronic disease screening has room for improvement; only 53% of Malays aged 40 to 74 attended chronic disease screening in 2023.

sections.label: Project Dian expansion to M3@Towns
sections.summary: Project Dian will expand to the remaining five M3@Towns by end-2025, covering all 11 M3@Towns and reaching 1000 more families in HDB rental homes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: With the success of this pilot project, I am pleased to announce that Project Dian will be expanded to the remaining five M3@Towns by end-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This means that Project Dian will be offered to all 11 M3@Towns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This expansion will allow us to reach out to 1000 more of these families living in HDB rental homes.

sections.label: Dian Ambassador programme expansion
sections.summary: The Dian Ambassador programme will be extended to all M3@Towns, training 100 more volunteers this year to supplement the current 200.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: With Project Dian’s expansion, we will progressively extend the Dian Ambassador programme to all M3@Towns, and train 100 more volunteers this year, to supplement the 200 volunteers that we have currently.

sections.label: Professionals guiding student leaders
sections.summary: 60 professionals aged 60 and above will provide guidance to 60 Malay/Muslim student leaders from neighbourhood secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In this project, 60 professionals aged 60 and above will provide guidance to 60 Malay/Muslim student leaders from neighbourhood secondary schools.

sections.label: RLAF Gaza fundraising
sections.summary: Over the past year and a half, the Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation has raised over $13 million and is now in its fourth fundraising campaign for Gaza.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Over the past year and a half, the Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation (RLAF) has raised over $13 million, and is now into its fourth fundraising campaign for Gaza.

sections.label: Campaign fundraising collection progress
sections.summary: The campaign collected $266,000 in its first two weeks, close to half of its $600,000 target.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In just the first two weeks of the campaign, we managed to collect $266,000, which is close to half of our target of $600,000 for this campaign.

sections.label: Malay educational and job gains
sections.summary: From 2000 to 2020, more Malay youths gained post-secondary qualifications, Malay graduates rose fivefold, and more Malays held PMET positions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: From 2000 to 2020, more than twice as many Malay youths obtained post-secondary or higher qualifications, rising from around 30% back in 2000 to around 80% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Among Malay adults, the proportion of university graduates has increased fivefold from 2.1% to 10.8%, and more Malays now hold PMET positions, with a steady rise from 23% to 40% in 2020.

sections.label: MTP centre and student growth
sections.summary: MTP has expanded to 100 centres across Singapore, with close to 9,700 students enrolled in 2024, a 35% increase over five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Today, MTP has expanded to 100 centres across Singapore, with close to 9,700 students enrolled in 2024, a 35% increase over the last five years.

sections.label: Training allowance amounts and eligibility
sections.summary: Full-time long-form trainees can get up to $3,000 monthly or $72,000 over two years, and part-time trainees $300 monthly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For those pursuing full-time long-form training, they can get a training allowance of up to $3,000 per month or up to $72,000 over two years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Government enhanced this initiative during this year’s Budget to include eligible participants of part-time training who will receive a training allowance of $300 per month.

sections.label: FA4 support for Malay/Muslim workers
sections.summary: FA4 has supported about 25,000 Malay/Muslim workers over three years through career fairs, job matching, skills development and mentoring.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Through collaboration with NTUC and community organisations, FA4 has supported about 25,000 Malay/Muslim workers through career fairs, job matching, skills development as well as mentoring programmes over the past three years. : Mr Chairman, we have also intensified efforts to prepare youths to enter the workforce.

sections.label: MENDAKI mentoring and professional networks
sections.summary: In 2024, #amPowered matched nearly 1,400 students to over 400 mentors, and Professional Networks cover 13 industries with over 850 members.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In 2024, MENDAKI's #amPowered programmes matched nearly 1,400 students to more than 400 mentors – double the number of mentors involved compared with 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Professional Networks now cover 13 different industries with a growing membership that has doubled to over 850 in the past year.

sections.label: MENDAKI corporate partner scholarships
sections.summary: Over five years, MENDAKI's corporate partners awarded around 45 scholarships for post-secondary education.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, MENDAKI's corporate partners have awarded around 45 scholarships to support students in their post-secondary education.

sections.label: First cohort graduates
sections.summary: The first cohort of 13 participants graduated in April 2024 and continue contributing nationally and in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The first cohort of 13 participants graduated in April 2024 and continue to contribute at national and community levels.

sections.label: Singapore College of Islamic Studies opening
sections.summary: The Singapore College of Islamic Studies is being set up and will open for an initial intake of 60 students in 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Today, we are fulfilling a long-standing aspiration of our community in setting up our Singapore College of Islamic Studies (SCIS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The SCIS will open its doors for an initial intake of 60 students in 2028.

sections.label: SCIS immersion programmes
sections.summary: Prospective students can participate in immersion programmes for applied learning in specialisations like Fatwa Studies, Quranic Studies, Social Work and Counselling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As part of the SCIS experience, prospective students can look forward to participating in immersion programmes for applied learning in specialisations across the SCIS' inter-disciplinary curriculum, such as Fatwa Studies, Quranic Studies, Social Work and Counselling.

sections.label: SCIS university partnerships
sections.summary: The SCIS will partner SUSS for its social sciences pathway and Islamic institutions for its Islamic studies pathway.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The SCIS will partner the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) for its social sciences pathway and with renowned Islamic institutions, such as Dar al-Ifta in Egypt, the University of Jordan and Al-Qarawiyyin in Morocco, for its Islamic studies pathway.

sections.label: SCIS Advisory Panel meeting
sections.summary: Leaders of partner institutions and universities like Al-Azhar will form the SCIS Advisory Panel, meeting first in Singapore in June 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Leaders of our partner institutions, together with other renowned universities like Al-Azhar, will be part of the SCIS' Advisory Panel.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: They will have their first meeting in Singapore in June 2025, on the sidelines of the International Conference on Cohesive Societies (ICCS).

sections.label: Mosque building in Tampines North and Tengah
sections.summary: The Prime Minister announced that development of the Tampines North mosque will resume and a new mosque will be built in Tengah in coming years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As our Prime Minister recently announced, we will resume developing the mosque in Tampines North and build a new mosque in Tengah in the coming years.

sections.label: Wakaf month campaign and WMS pledgers
sections.summary: MUIS held its inaugural Wakaf month campaign last August, raised $6.25 million so far, and will launch an SG60 campaign to reach 6,000 WMS pledgers by year end.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To raise awareness of WMS, MUIS held its inaugural Wakaf month campaign last August and will do so again this July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am pleased to report that we have raised $6.25 million so far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In conjunction with SG60, MUIS will launch a campaign to increase the number of pledgers to WMS to 6,000 individuals by the end of the year.

sections.label: Asatizah recognised under ARS
sections.summary: There are 5,080 asatizah recognised under the Asatizah Recognition Scheme, of which around two-thirds are female.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To Mr Faisal Manap’s query, there are 5,080 asatizah recognised under the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS), of which around two-thirds are female.

sections.label: Madrasah admissions and asatizah salaries
sections.summary: Madrasahs can admit up to 400 students per Primary 1 cohort, and since 2023 over 80% of asatizah in mosques and madrasahs received salary increases of 5% to 12% to meet the Common Salary Guideline.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To Mr Faisal Manap’s query, for each Primary 1 cohort, our madrasahs can admit up to 400 students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: One key strategy to grow the attractiveness of our asatizah sector is the phased implementation of a Common Salary Guideline (CSG), as recommended by the Committee of Future Asatizah (COFA) earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since 2023, we have raised the salaries of more than 80% of asatizah working in our mosques and madrasahs to meet the CSG salary range, with an increase in their salaries ranging between an average of 5% to 12%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: With the third phase of implementation this year, I hope to bring more of our asatizah to within the CSG salary range.

sections.label: ICCOS 2024 recognition of Malay/Muslim community
sections.summary: At ICCOS in October 2024, regional and international audiences were impressed by how the Malay/Muslim community practises Islam in context and expressed interest in learning from its journey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: At the second edition of the International Conference on Communities of Success (ICCOS) in October 2024, regional and international audiences were deeply impressed by how our Malay/Muslim community practise Islam in context, harmonising faith with Singapore’s rich multicultural society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Many expressed keen interests in learning from our journey, inspired by how we have navigated challenges and embraced opportunities to thrive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This recognition reaffirms our approach in building Communities of Success, strengthening our confidence to contribute meaningfully to the development of similar communities around the world.

sections.label: KMM programme evaluation results
sections.summary: With a programme evaluation office in MENDAKI, studies show nine in 10 kids who went through KMM for a reasonable period no longer required the Learning Support for Mathematics programme in primary school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: First, now that we have established a programme evaluation office in MENDAKI, we are tracking closely and we have done studies internally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: That is how we have come up with results that nine in 10 kids in who have gone through KMM for a reasonable period no longer required the Learning Support for Mathematics (LSM) programme in primary school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: When we started KMM, it was only about 300 students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We are now covering about 3,000 students and parents.

sections.label: Longitudinal studies with IPS
sections.summary: A data platform is being used with the Institute of Policy Studies to do longitudinal studies on how this affects children over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The second thing we are doing is, given that we now have a data platform, we are now working with the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS), doing longitudinal studies on how this affects our kids and how they perform over time.

sections.label: OPG at Bulan Wakaf
sections.summary: At the Bulan Wakaf in August last year, the Office of the Public Guardian spoke about wills and the Lasting Power of Attorney.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For example, at the Bulan Wakaf that we celebrated in August last year, the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) was actually there, not just to tell the community that it is important to have a will, but also to talk about what you should do even before you pass on, like having a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), and so on.

sections.label: Double applications for Primary 1 places
sections.summary: There are 400 Primary 1 enrolment places each year, and almost every year there is a double application for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: If I were to hear the Minister mentioned correctly just now that there are 400 places every year for Primary 1 enrolment and, at this point in time, almost every year, we have a double application for that 400 places.

sections.label: Madrasah numbers and national system
sections.summary: Of 400 admitted yearly to madrasah, about 150 go on to Islamic tertiary education, and the 400 number fits manpower planning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Today, out of the 400 annually that we admit into madrasah, actually only around 150 move on to do Islamic tertiary education beyond our madrasah system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: If we had not designed our madrasah so that if they were to leave the madrasah system or cannot complete the madrasah system, they can go back to the national system, we would have a situation that we had before the year 2000 – many drop-outs who would not be able to get back into the national system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: But because, over the years, we have constrained the numbers or limited the numbers to fit the needs of the community, the number of asatizahs we need in the years to come and we have done the manpower planning for that, 400 is about just nice.

sections.label: 400 asatizah places sufficient
sections.summary: The 400 places are sufficient for now, and will be increased over time if more are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We do not want to end up with our asatizah pursuing a very long journey in becoming a religious scholar, finding no place in our society or mostly freelancing for that matter, while they do other jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: So, for now, this 400 is sufficient, it is what we need and, over time, if we need more, we will certainly increase it.

sections.label: Twenty percent mosque guideline
sections.summary: Twenty percent was a guideline, being about the right amount for the mosque to support the executive chairman's deployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Twenty percent was just a guideline, because that is about the right amount to get the mosque to support the deployment of the executive chairman.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim community health efforts
sections.summary: Efforts continue to improve Malay/Muslim community health, including Healthier SG sign-ups, preventive healthcare and chronic illness, with JKJU reaching out via community resources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Indeed, we continue to pay attention to the health of the Malay/Muslim community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman

sections.summary: NAC will scale up arts access to 70% of Government-supported preschools in 2025 and 100% by 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In 2025, NAC will scale up to 70% of Government-supported preschools, around 700 schools, and eventually reach 100% of the preschools by 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This means nearly 1,000 preschools and 44,000 students will have access to quality arts learning experiences.

sections.label: Enhanced arts scholarships funding
sections.summary: MCCY and NAC will allocate an additional $2 million yearly for arts scholarships, including a new NAC Creative Arts Scholarship.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: MCCY and NAC will certainly enhance our arts scholarships this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We will allocate an additional $2 million per year for arts scholarships, allowing us to award more NAC Arts Scholarships for undergraduate and postgraduate studies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This funding will also go towards a new NAC Creative Arts Scholarship for pre-tertiary and diploma studies offered by School of the Arts, Singapore (SOTA), the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA) as well as LASALLE.

sections.label: Arts Management Leadership Programme pilot
sections.summary: NAC will pilot an Arts Management Leadership Programme for emerging and mid-career arts managers with mentorship, coaching, leadership programmes and attachments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: NAC will pilot an Arts Management Leadership Programme for emerging and mid-career arts managers to undergo mentorship and coaching, milestone leadership programmes and industry attachments.

sections.label: SG Heritage Business Scheme pilot
sections.summary: MCCY will pilot the SG Heritage Business Scheme to recognise exemplary heritage businesses and boost demand for their products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We have set up an inter-agency task force on this issue.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This year, MCCY will pilot the SG Heritage Business Scheme to recognise exemplary heritage businesses and help boost demand for such products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Businesses that have been operating for at least 30 years, providing locally rooted trades, goods, or services, and contribute significantly to the identity of community or place, can be designated as "SG Heritage Businesses".

sections.label: Initiative audience at venues
sections.summary: The initiative has attracted over 40,000 audience since its launch last year, featuring performances by cultural groups such as Ding Yi.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: From Heartbeat@Bedok to Kampung Admiralty, the initiative has attracted over 40,000 audience since its launch last year, featuring performances by various cultural groups, such as Chinese ensemble, Ding Yi.

sections.label: Co-op movement centenary year
sections.summary: This year, Singapore celebrates the centenary year of its co-operative societies, or co-ops.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: I am speaking, of course, of our co-operative societies, or "co-ops" for short.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This year, we celebrate the centenary year of our co-op movement here in Singapore.

sections.label: Co-op fund contributions waived
sections.summary: This year, first-tier Central Co-operative Fund contributions are waived for co-ops, helping over 60 co-ops, with a 10-year transformation roadmap consultation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: They were celebrating their 60th anniversary and we discussed how best to support co-ops like them, and I told them to listen out for today's COS debate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This year, we will waive the first-tier Central Co-operative Fund contributions for co-ops.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Co-ops contribute part of their yearly surplus to the Fund, which supports their development and growth in areas like education, training and research.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This waiver that I just announced will help over 60 co-ops.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: They can choose to redirect these savings to enhance their social mission or to better cope with rising costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: And together with the Singapore National Co-operative Federation, we will also launch a consultation with the sector to develop a transformation roadmap for the next 10 years.

sections.label: Delegates below 35 years
sections.summary: Over a quarter of the delegates will be below 35 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Over a quarter of our delegates will be below 35 years old.

sections.label: ICCS 2025 harmony perspectives
sections.summary: ICCS 2025, the third edition, will bring participants to places of worship and heritage districts to witness diverse religious and cultural practices coexisting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: I shared how Singapore, through our example and platforms like ICCS, can contribute perspectives on striving for harmony in an increasingly divided world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: So, ICCS 2025, the third edition, will bring participants to our iconic places of worship and heritage districts to witness diverse religious and cultural practices coexisting harmoniously in shared spaces across Singapore.

sections.label: Alliance for Integration of Foreign Professionals
sections.summary: This year, MCCY is partnering the business community to convene an Alliance for Acrton on Integration of Foreign Professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: I agree we should do more, beginning at our workplaces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Therefore, this year, MCCY is partnering our business community to convene an Alliance for Acrton (AfA) on Integration of Foreign Professionals.

sections.label: OCBC Singapore Immersion Programme run
sections.summary: Last year, OCBC organised its inaugural Singapore Immersion Programme, providing foreign employees opportunities to get involved in the community alongside local colleagues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Last year, OCBC organised their inaugural run of the Singapore Immersion Programme (SIP), which provides opportunities for foreign employees to get involved in the community alongside their local colleagues.

sections.label: Youths' four policy papers
sections.summary: The youths spent over a year developing ideas across four panels, engaged over 5,000 peers, and distilled views into four policy papers with 11 recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The youths spent over a year developing their ideas across these four panels and engaged over 5,000 of their peers through surveys, focus group discussions and our Youth Policy Forum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: They then distilled their views into four policy papers with 11 recommendations.

sections.label: GreenHacks recycling panel recommendations
sections.summary: Kimberly led a #GreenHacks panel proposing segregated recycling bins and standardised labels, and the recommendations are being considered.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In fact, Kimberly led our #GreenHacks panel to propose solutions like segregated recycling bins and standardised recycling labels, to improve consumer knowledge and promote better recycling habits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We are considering the Panels' recommendations and will respond soon.

sections.label: Partners joining the movement
sections.summary: Over 260 partners, including corporates, mentoring organisations and community groups, have joined the movement since its 2022 launch.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Over 260 partners – which involves corporates, mentoring organisations, community groups – have joined the movement since we launched it in 2022.

sections.label: Disability sports participation and taskforce
sections.summary: Sports participation among persons with disabilities rose from 28% in 2015 to 45% in 2024, and a refreshed masterplan targets 70% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Since then, we have seen an increase in sports participation rates amongst persons with disabilities, from 28% in 2015 to 45% in 2024, and our para-sports athletes have also consistently performed well at major games.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We set up the Enabling Sports Taskforce, engaged stakeholders and launched a refreshed masterplan last November, which aims to raise sports participation rate of persons with disabilities to 70% by 2030.

sections.label: Awareness of disability sports
sections.summary: Initiatives like Play Inclusive will be expanded, and all mainstream school students will experience at least one disability sport by 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Second, we will raise awareness of disability sports and inclusive sports activities by expanding initiatives, like Play Inclusive, so that all Singaporeans can play and enjoy sports together, regardless of ability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This includes working with MOE to have all students in mainstream schools experience at least one disability sports by 2028.

sections.label: New Enabling Sports Fund
sections.summary: Based on engagement feedback, a new Enabling Sports Fund will launch in the second half of this year to support community disability sports initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Lastly, based on feedback from our engagement sessions, we will launch a new Enabling Sports Fund in the second half of this year to support more community initiatives in disability sports.

sections.label: CALM programme and adaptive equipment
sections.summary: 54 Active Ageing Centres have completed the CALM programme, with aims to double this and provide adaptive sports equipment to about 100 centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To date, 54 Active Ageing Centres have completed the CALM programme and we aim to double this to about 100 Active Ageing Centres by end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We also aim to provide adaptive sports equipment to about 100 Active Ageing Centres by end of this year too.

sections.label: Sports Facilities Master Plan progress
sections.summary: Three sport centres have been renovated and 15 committed development projects completed under the Sports Facilities Master Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To-date, we have renovated three sport centres and completed 15 of our committed development projects, as part of our Sports Facilities Master Plan.

sections.label: SIP facilities completed and pipeline
sections.summary: Ten SIP facilities have been completed, with another 24 in the pipeline.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To date, we have completed 10 SIP facilities, with another 24 in the pipeline.

sections.label: Inclusion in sports and Paralympic medals
sections.summary: The speaker joined Singapore para-athletes in Paris and says true inclusion means common spaces where all feel welcomed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Last summer, I was privileged to have joined Jeralyn and Pin Xiu and Team Singapore para-athletes in Paris, as they brought home an historic haul of Paralympic medals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: I am extremely proud of all of them and I am also sure that they will agree with me when I say that true inclusion in sports is not merely about catering carve-outs for persons with disabilities or for our seniors for that matter.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: It is about creating common spaces where all, regardless of age, abilities and persuasions, feel welcomed, respected and valued.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Sport has always been a powerful force for unity, transcending differences, bridging divides.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: By fostering inclusion in every game, every match and every Singaporean journey, we can weave a stronger fabric of diversity into the very DNA of Singapore society.

sections.label: No grants for commercial event
sections.summary: No Government grants were given; the event was a purely commercial arrangement between the artist and the venue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: No Government grants were given to secure this event.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This was a purely commercial arrangement between the artist and the venue, and an agreement was entered into.

sections.label: Studying museum site feasibility
sections.summary: The feasibility of the site for such a museum is being studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I said, we are studying the feasibility of the site for such a museum.

sections.label: Artworks left out of Culture Pass
sections.summary: Because art is less of an investment, artwork purchase was left out of the Culture Pass programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is less of an investment, unlike visual art.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And so, we decided that, given the policy around Culture Pass to create more of a community around appreciation, where you can come together and you can partake in the appreciation as a group, we felt that it was more appropriate to leave the purchase of artworks out of this programme.

sections.label: Arts employment structure versus social service
sections.summary: The arts sector's employment structure differs greatly from the social service sector's salary guidelines, as arts practitioners differentiate themselves through unique artistic vision and practice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For example, in the arts, work is highly differentiated and variable, and our arts and culture practitioners generally differentiate themselves through the uniqueness of the vision for the art piece or the performance, as well as the artistic practice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: So, while the National Council of Social Service's salary guidelines for the social service sector set pay benchmarks for specific roles and responsibility in the social service sector, employment structure, in comparison, for the arts and cultural sector, differs quite greatly.

sections.label: Arts and Culture Employment Survey
sections.summary: NAC conducts the Arts and Culture Employment Survey, and its 2024 findings will be released later this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Allow me to also reassure Ms Usha Chandradas that NAC also conducts what we call the Arts and Culture Employment Survey, which surveys the arts workforce and organisation, and I am happy to share with her that the 2024 findings will be released later this year.

sections.label: Heritage Activation Nodes programme
sections.summary: NHB launched HAN to engage communities in heritage, with HAN@Katong-Joo Chiat and HAN@Clementi, drawing over 9,900 participants, 2,050 volunteers and 50 partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: NHB has launched HAN since last year to engage communities in exploring and also celebrating heritage through collaborative projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And the first two that we have launched since the announcement last year are: one, HAN@Katong-Joo Chiat, because it showcases Katong-Joo Chiat's very interesting multicultural heritage, especially Peranakan influences, traditional architecture, as well as food culture; the second one, launched at Dr Tan Wu Meng's ward, HAN@Clementi, in September 2024, engages the youths in uncovering hidden heritage gems through schools and also community collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Over this project, we are happy to update Ms Hany Soh that more than 9,900 people have joined the HAN programme with more than 2,050 new heritage volunteers and 50 partners on board.

sections.label: Kallang Alive residential facilities
sections.summary: Residential facilities at Kallang Alive will house the Sports School with training centres, to bring foreign coaches and teams to train and spar in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As we move closer towards that, we will also have residential facilities at the Kallang Alive space, where the Sports School will sit together with our training centres, and the intention is not just to bring foreign coaches to come in and train with us, but also foreign teams to come in, site in Singapore and spar with us on a more regular basis.

sections.label: Expanding sports programmes at Kallang Alive
sections.summary: When the Sports School at Kallang Alive is redeveloped, programmes will expand beyond 10, with top-tier sports selected based on performance, pipeline and other criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We currently have limitations in terms of space, given the programmes, some of which Mr Giam is aware of.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But when we have the Sports School at the Kallang Alive Masterplan space ready, redeveloped, we intend to expand beyond 10 programmes, and we are currently studying which of our top-tier sports ought to train in this space, having regard to performance, pipeline and other criteria for each of the sports.

sections.label: Company of Good recognition growth
sections.summary: The speaker sits on NVPC's Company of Good Roundtable and has seen more companies value the recognition, including a four-fold increase in SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In fact, I sit on the NVPC's Company of Good Roundtable and we meet very regularly and have seen an increase in the number of companies that value the Company of Good's recognition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: That is why we have seen not just a number of companies, large local companies, and MNCs, being on board, but also see a four-fold increase in the number of SMEs.

sections.label: MyCareersFuture options open
sections.summary: Nothing is off the table regarding MyCareersFuture, in response to Ms Jean See's question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As to Ms Jean See's other question with regard to MyCareersFuture, nothing is off the table.

sections.label: Inter-agency taskforce on heritage businesses
sections.summary: Two co-chaired taskforce meetings identified an initial group of probably 150 heritage businesses, involving MND, MCCY, MTI and Enterprise Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Together with my fellow Parliamentarian, Minister of State Faisal Ibrahim, both of us had co-chaired two taskforce meetings on this inter-agency taskforce, involving not just the MND family, not just the MCCY, but also including the Ministry of Trade and Industry, and Enterprise Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We have identified that there will be an initial group of probably 150 heritage businesses.

sections.label: Merging SSI with NYSI
sections.summary: SSI and NYSI will merge to harness synergy and economies of scale, serving the same number of athletes, if not more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Is participation in these programmes chargeable, and how do we ensure that these programmes are accessible to all seniors, including those who are less mobile who live alone, who do not come to the Active Ageing Centres in the first instance?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We intend to rationalise and strengthen the sporting support and as you heard me say in my speech earlier, we intend to first merge SSI with NYSI, and both of them support the athlete, one in the junior level, the other at the senior level, but the technical support – sports science, nutrition, sports medicine, we intend to harness the synergy as well as the economies of scale for both of these agencies into one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will be serving the same number of athletes, if not more at the junior level, as well as at the senior level.

sections.label: Free Active Ageing programmes
sections.summary: The two programmes at Active Ageing Centres are free, and seniors can also participate at Active Health Labs in Active SG Sports Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The two programmes that are offered at the Active Ageing Centres are free of charge, but outside of the Active Ageing Centres, seniors can also participate in these two programmes at the Active Health Labs, which are located in the Active SG Sports Centres.

sections.label: Youths in interfaith space
sections.summary: Youths have formed youth sector organisations such as Rose of Peace and hash.peace, and many will be involved with ICCS 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: First, it is really encouraging to see our youths stepping up in the interfaith space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I mentioned this was something that we have done in previous generations, but this new generation of youths, they have new ideas, they have formed many of these youth sector organisations – Rose of Peace is one; hash.peace is another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: If you noticed during the recent visit of the Pope last year, there were many youths involved, including Shukul Raaj Kumar, who is 29 years old and led the interfaith youth discussions at the Catholic Junior College with the Pope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Many of them will be involved with ICCS 2025.

sections.label: Refreshing INC training and branding
sections.summary: MCCY refreshed the IRCC into Harmony Circles and will look at training, recruitment and refreshing INC's branding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MCCY has refreshed, for example, the IRCC into the Harmony Circles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We think that it is an appropriate time for us to also look at what we can do better in terms of training, recruitment and also refreshing the branding of INC so that they are more relevant to what we have today.
